pointers.sentence: A project that defines them and no `MAILERS` still sends mail through them (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:get_connection`).
An email setting that the settings module defines warns as the module loads (`django/conf/__init__.py:Settings.__init__`).
Setting and reading warn only from code outside Django, so a value that Django's own code read first warns no later reader (`django/conf/__init__.py:_show_settings_deprecation_warning`).

A settings module that defines an email setting beside `MAILERS` is refused with `ImproperlyConfigured`, and so is one call of `LazySettings.configure` given both (`django/conf/__init__.py:_check_email_settings_conflicts`).
Where `MAILERS` is defined, an email setting cannot be read, even one left at its default (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__getattr__`).
Where no tags are named either, it leaves out the checks tagged database (`django/core/checks/registry.py:CheckRegistry.run_checks`).

A field's backend checks ask MySQL's backend for the field's column type (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field._check_backend_specific_checks`), and the backend connects to learn its features (`django/db/backends/mysql/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.mysql_server_data`).

A field's backend checks ask MySQL's backend for the field's column type (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field._check_backend_specific_checks`), and the backend connects to learn its features (`django/db/backends/mysql/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.mysql_server_data`).
The notes say that callers "should be prepared for databases to be accessed" (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`; [The system checks](../commands/checks.md)).

Since 5.2 `BaseCommand.execute` takes its arguments for `BaseCommand.check` from `BaseCommand.get_check_kwargs`, which a command may override (`django/core/management/base.py:BaseCommand.get_check_kwargs`).
The migrate command adds its database; runserver runs the checks itself as it starts serving, with no database named (`django/core/management/commands/runserver.py:Command.inner_run`).
`Settings.__init__` turns an `ImportError` that names the settings module itself into `ImproperlyConfigured` (`django/conf/__init__.py:Settings.__init__`), which `ManagementUtility.execute` keeps.

`ManagementUtility.fetch_command` then refuses a command whose `BaseCommand.requires_settings` is true, with the exception's message (`django/core/management/__init__.py:ManagementUtility.fetch_command`).
Until 6.2 `execute` kept an `ImportError` too and ran the command, which failed with a traceback if it read a setting (`django/core/management/__init__.py:ManagementUtility.execute`).
The 6.2 notes say `requires_settings` makes configurable "whether to suppress an ImportError escaping from a settings module" (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`).

In 6.0 the settings module that startproject writes lost `DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD` (`django/conf/project_template/project_name/settings.py-tpl`), and the configuration class that startapp writes lost `AppConfig.default_auto_field`.
Both had named `BigAutoField`, which 6.0 made the default (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`).
Since 6.0 both commands make a missing target directory, parents and all, where 5.2.17 refused (`django/core/management/templates.py:TemplateCommand.handle`).
Since 5.2 the shell fills its namespace before it starts, from the dotted paths that `Command.get_auto_imports` returns (`django/core/management/commands/shell.py:Command.get_auto_imports`).

| a mistyped choice | Since 6.1, on Python 3.14, argparse's error offers the nearest choice | `django/core/management/base.py:CommandParser.__init__` |

| listurls | New in 6.2: the command that lists the root URLconf's URLs ([The URL checks, and listing the patterns](../urls/checks.md)) | `django/core/management/commands/listurls.py:Command.handle` |
| the debug context processor | Since 5.2, left out of the `TEMPLATES` that startproject writes, and still in Django | `django/template/context_processors.py:debug` |
